info.description: The API behind the 學益 webapp. Generated from the backend_new route definitions by tools/openapi.ts -- do not edit by hand.

get.description: Touches no table, so it keeps answering 200 while the database is unreachable. This is what the load balancer reads.

get.summary: List the subscription plans and their prices
get.description: Public and unauthenticated, because the pricing page is read before signing in. These are the authoritative amounts: the figure shown has to be the figure signed into the ECPay order, so a client must not hold prices of its own.

amount.description: NTD. The authoritative price: a client must render this, never a constant of its own

days.description: Days of access, added to whatever the caller already has

get.description: Every published payout, with the arithmetic a reader needs to check it against the receipt linked from its evidence: donationCount x donationUnitAmount + platformTopUp equals transferredAmount. Public and unauthenticated on purpose -- being readable by anyone is the whole of its value as proof. It names no user; a batch is the smallest unit shown.

200.description: The running totals, and one page of published batches

maxedSpiritCount.description: Spirits grown to max level -- every one of them is owed

confirmedAmount.description: Summed from the frozen per-donation amounts

pendingCount.description: Maxed, but the owner has not picked an organisation yet

pendingAmount.description: pendingCount x donationAmount -- the only figure here priced at today's rate

promisedAmount.description: confirmedAmount + pendingAmount, so a reader can check it

transferredAmount.description: Over published batches only, so the listed batches add up to it

donationAmount.description: Today's figure, which prices pendingAmount and nothing else

reference.description: Bank transaction number, or the last digits of the account

donationUnitAmount.description: The one frozen amount every member shares, or null when they differ; null means the multiplication must not be printed

platformTopUp.description: transferredAmount - donationSubtotal. Signed: negative would mean the batch sent less than was promised

get.summary: Suggest an organisation in a category
get.description: Reads here need no credentials: the name, blurb and website of a foundation are what the public transparency page exists to show. `adminAuth` gates POST/PUT/DELETE only. Answers with the **least-supported** active organisation in the category -- least by summed donation amount, with sortOrder then id breaking ties, so an untouched category answers the same for everyone. It exists because the choice is the emotional payoff of the LV5 donation and therefore a wall for anyone without an opinion; it is a suggestion, not a hidden choice inside POST /api/donation, because the public record names the organisation and the user has to see who it is before confirming.

post.summary: Find or create the caller from their Firebase identity
post.description: Called on every sign-in; the only thing that ever creates a user row, which is why it is the one route here not behind requireUser. Returns 201 when it created the row. Only lastLoginAt is refreshed for a returning user -- a changed name or avatar on the Firebase side is not written back. The caller's subscription comes with it so sign-in needs one authenticated request rather than two.

Scoring, the points award, the per-subject statistics and the wrong-question list are all written here, and a question scoring below 10 is added to that list automatically.

type.description: GROUP, SINGLE, MULTIPLE, TRUE_FALSE, FILL or CLOZE. Every write validates against those six; the column is a varchar, so a reader should not assume it

children.description: Empty unless this is a 題組; the children of one carry the questions

score.description: 0-10, from the most recent wrong attempt

wrongCount.description: How many times this has gone wrong

entries.description: In the order the sub-questions appear in the paper, not by when each went wrong

total.description: Rows matching the query, ignoring limit and offset

totalPages.description: At least 1, so an empty result reads as "page 1 of 1" rather than "of 0"

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed filter

put.summary: Write or clear the note on one wrong sub-question
put.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller: a row belonging to someone else reads as 404 rather than 403, so this never confirms that a given id exists for another user. `note: null` clears it.

200.description: The id, the note as saved, and when

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601. Always set -- this response is the write that just happened

400.description: note missing, or longer than 2000 characters

404.description: No such row belongs to this caller

delete.summary: Remove one wrong sub-question from the list
delete.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller. Answering it wrong again puts it back -- POST /api/reply re-adds anything scoring below 10.

404.description: No such row belongs to this caller

get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller: there is no way to read anyone else's. Newest first, ordered by id rather than createdAt -- a POST /reply batch writes several rows sharing one timestamp, so id is the only column that keeps their order.

200.description: One page of movements, newest first

type.description: EARN_REPLY, SPEND_EGG_REDEEM and the rest -- a varchar rather than an enum, so a new kind of movement needs no schema change

replyId.description: The reply this came from, for anything earned by answering

balanceAfter.description: The running balance once this had been applied

total.description: Rows matching the query, ignoring limit and offset

totalPages.description: At least 1, so an empty result reads as "page 1 of 1" rather than "of 0"

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed offset

get.summary: The guardian catalog, with owner counts per level
get.description: Behind requireAdmin -- every method, GET included. `adminAuth` would have been no protection at all here, since it only gates POST/PUT/DELETE and this resource has none. GET-only on purpose: a species is half a row and half a set of artwork files keyed by `code`, so creating one through an API would only ever produce a row with no pictures.

200.description: Every species, retired ones included, ordered by sortOrder then id

code.description: What the frontend keys this species' artwork by

theme.description: The egg's own label, which is not the category link below

isActive.description: Whether it is still on sale; owners of a retired one keep it

category.description: The donation category this species supports, or null for one tied to none. null is both what the planned VIP spirit is and what a seeded egg looks like when its category_id was forgotten -- indistinguishable from here, which is why the admin page says it out loud.

ownersByLevel.description: Owners keyed by the level they have grown to. An absent level has no owners; the caller decides which levels to show. Keys are strings because JSON object keys are.

get.summary: The species on sale, and which of them the caller owns
get.description: Behind requireUser. Active species only, unlike the admin catalog at GET /api/species: a retired one still exists for whoever owns it, but it is not on sale.

200.description: The shelf, and the balance to spend on it

code.description: What the frontend keys this species' artwork by

level.description: How far this species has been grown, or null when not owned. The collection view needs the level and not just `owned`: it shows progress per species and sorts the started ones first.

totalPoints.description: The caller's balance, so the shelf needs no second call

post.description: Behind requireUser. Spends `cost` points and hatches the egg at level 1. Only `totalPoints` is decremented, never `lifetimePoints`, so redeeming never costs leaderboard rank.

200.description: The new spirit and the balance left

id.description: The new user_guardian row, not the species

totalPoints.description: The balance after the cost was taken

400.description: Already owned (ALREADY_OWNED) or not enough points (INSUFFICIENT_POINTS) -- the code in the body says which

404.description: No such species, or it is not on sale

get.description: Every spirit this user owns, with the caller's point balance.

nextLevelXp.description: XP this spirit still needs for its next level, or null at the maximum

category.description: The public-interest category this species supports, or null for one tied to none

post.description: Spends the full `points` and adds XP, levelling the spirit up as many times as the XP covers. Paid access earns a growth bonus, which the server decides for itself from the caller's entitlement -- the request body cannot ask for it.

200.description: The spirit after the investment, the new balance, and the XP granted

nextLevelXp.description: XP this spirit still needs for its next level, or null at the maximum

category.description: The public-interest category this species supports, or null for one tied to none

xpGained.description: XP actually granted, growth bonus included

400.description: Already at the maximum level, or not enough points

404.description: No such spirit belongs to this caller

get.description: Behind requireUser, and scoped to the caller. Carries `userGuardianId` so the client can tell which of its maxed spirits have already chosen: this list and GET /api/guardian are what the picker is built from.

200.description: One page of donations, newest first by default

userGuardianId.description: Which maxed spirit paid for it -- how the picker knows one is spent

amount.description: Frozen at confirmation. Never render the current donationAmount in its place

published.description: Whether the public page shows this batch yet. A donation can be paid before its evidence is uploaded, and this record should not link to a batch nobody can read.

batch.description: null while the money has not gone out yet -- there is no status column

total.description: Rows matching the query, ignoring limit and offset

totalPages.description: At least 1, so an empty result reads as "page 1 of 1" rather than "of 0"

donationAmount.description: What confirming one more spirit would be worth. The figure a *new* donation would freeze, which is why every row above carries its own amount instead.

400.description: limit beyond the cap, or a malformed offset or order

post.summary: Confirm which organisation one maxed spirit supports
post.description: Behind requireUser. Irreversible by design: `donation.user_guardian_id` is UNIQUE, so one spirit means one donation forever. `categoryId` is required only for a species tied to no category (the VIP spirit, whose owner may direct the donation anywhere); for any other spirit the only legal value is its own category, so it can be left out.

404.description: No such spirit belongs to this caller, or no such organisation. Someone else's spirit reads as not-found rather than forbidden: whether a given id exists is not this caller's business

get.summary: What is still owed to one foundation
get.description: Admin only. The starting point of a payout: donations for this organisation with no batch yet (`donation.batch_id` NULL is the entire state machine -- there is no status column). Paginated, so `summary` reports the whole unpaid set rather than the page.

The body carries the file as base64 (with or without a `data:` prefix); it is uploaded to S3 under `donations/{batchId}/` and the row keeps the key.
